note: The platform this library promises to work on, and every feature used below that line. A feature below the floor is allowed only with a fallback that a check demonstrates — the allowlist is also the documentation of what somebody under the floor loses.

floor.means: In the Baseline sense: interoperable across Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari for at least 30 months. A feature that reached that line needs no entry here.

roles.load-bearing: Something a person cannot do at all without it. Needs a fallback that leaves the same capability reachable by another route.
roles.enhancement: Something that looks or feels better with it. Needs a fallback that degrades rather than breaks, and the entry says what is lost.

allowed.lost: The popup is laid out in the page rather than the top layer, so an ancestor with a transform or a clipping overflow can cut it. It still opens, closes, positions against its trigger and dismisses.
allowed.fallback: `hidden` carries the open state on its own, and every call is wrapped: a missing method, a disconnected element and a refusal from the platform all leave the popup showing rather than taking the field down.

allowed.lost: A translucent surface is drawn as a solid one. Nothing moves and nothing becomes unreadable.
allowed.fallback: Every use sits inside `@supports`, with the solid colour declared outside it.

allowed.lost: The secondary, tertiary and error colours are not derived from the primary one; the palette's declared defaults are used instead.
allowed.fallback: Every use sits inside `@supports`, with the fixed palette declared outside it.
